# Soft sprites

@difference Extension: `SetSpriteSoftEdge` fades see-through sprites out where they get close to solid geometry (soft particles); the original has no such command.

Sprites are flat squares, so where one is partly inside a wall or the ground the sprite is cut off along a hard line. [SetSpriteSoftEdge](SetSpriteSoftEdge) fades the sprite over a distance given in world units. On the GPU the renderer first draws everything solid, then the sprites with the depth buffer of the solid things readable by the sprite shader: the difference between the distance of the sprite and the distance of the solid surface behind it, divided by the soft edge distance and limited to 0 to 1, is multiplied into the alpha of the sprite. The depth is not copied, the same buffer is both the depth test and the image that is sampled, which is why this only costs something for scenes that use the command (one extra pass boundary and one depth texture read per pixel of those sprites).
